A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the participants' emotional capital, which was often a response to the fear of complaint, was not a resource that they were able to mobilise in order to gain the most from the healthcare system.

the participants in this study had to work hard to maintain their emotional capital and this was achieved by a combination of strategies that involved deflecting blame, deflecting anger and deflecting complaint.
the experience of surgical infections is a source of considerable emotional distress and that this is often managed by the deployment of emotional capital.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the experience of surgical infections is not just one of suffering but also of the management of suffering.

patients with surgical site infections are often reluctant to blame healthcare institutions for the infections, and this may contribute to the low levels of complaints and litigation that are reported.
